characters.name: Juan Carlos
characters.description: First-person narrator; sound artist in the Bronx; eats a vending-machine lunch in the Concourse library while researching spirals; runs a Chismosa check that triggers an echo of the 1934 reading room; scored 'level two' on the Calm Index as a child; walks home past the bodega despite Sofía's warning. Physical appearance unspecified.
characters.evidence:
I sat there, a man in a hoodie with a ginger ale, in a room that had
been dead for ninety years

characters.name: Sofía
characters.description: Runs the tenant association's research; has 'two settings, asleep and prosecuting'; digs into Aperture Civic's shells, the music-licensing installs, and the 2007 Quiet Hours Foundation grant; demands a control block and warns JC not to reply to the email or walk past the bodega. Physical appearance unspecified.
characters.evidence:
because Sofía has two settings, asleep and pro‐
secuting.

characters.name: Denise
characters.description: Mentioned-only (via text message); works at the arts space; informs JC the board is holding his milestone payment until the partner review. Physical appearance unspecified.
characters.evidence: Denise: Hi JC! Quick heads up, the board is holding your milestone payment until

characters.name: Manny
characters.description: Mentioned-only; musician friend; JC hears his voice saying 'it'll cost you'; bet Sofía a dollar about browser tabs. Physical appearance unspecified.
characters.evidence: Manny was going to be unbearable.

characters.name: The snoring man in the library
characters.description: Unnamed library patron near the radiator whose snoring JC considers 'a public service'; still snoring when the echo ends. Physical appearance unspecified.
characters.evidence:
near a man who was snoring in a way I considered a public
service.

characters.name: The narrator's grandmother
characters.description: Lives in Santo Domingo; keeps a wrapped bundle in the back of her closet; caught young JC's wrist with 'No se toca a la Madre' and gave him a mango; gave him the coin at twelve. Appears in flashback; not called in the present. Physical appearance unspecified.
characters.evidence: “No se toca a la Madre,” she said.

characters.name: The 1934 reading room crowd
characters.description: Collective ensemble in the echo: a grandfather with a Yiddish newspaper, two Irish girls splitting an apple, a man in a porter's cap reading slow with a finger under the line, a Puerto Rican mother steering two kids to picture books, a boy copying a world map, a darker-skinned boy borrowing his eraser, and a librarian with spectacles on a chain stamping a book. Individual physical details as listed; otherwise unspecified.
characters.evidence:
Under
the same green lamps sat a grandfather with a newspaper in Yiddish,

characters.name: Adrian Vale
characters.description: Mentioned-only (in an online photo); tall, gray, courteous man in a good coat at a ribbon-cutting, holding oversized scissors and a small black notebook he carries in every photo; signed JC's email. Note: not automatically the character labeled VALE on the style board.
characters.evidence:
a tall, gray, courteous man in a good coat at a ribbon-cutting, a
pair of oversized scissors in one hand and a small black notebook in the
other.

characters.name: Mr. Rodríguez
characters.description: Mentioned-only; café owner who told the music-system rep to take the speaker back and plays his own records; his café becomes the control for Sofía's comparison. Physical appearance unspecified.
characters.evidence:
Mr. Rodríguez told their rep to take the
speaker back to whatever planet it came from.

characters.name: The elementary school teacher
characters.description: Mentioned-only (in flashback); ran after-lunch quiet time under the classroom speaker and wrote down JC's desk-tapping. Physical appearance unspecified.
characters.evidence: That was what the teacher wrote down.

characters.name: The woman with a lanyard
characters.description: Unnamed observer in the school flashback who watched JC with a clipboard; a week later a letter came home. Physical appearance unspecified.
characters.evidence: I know because a woman with a lanyard came one afternoon and watched me with a clipboard,

characters.name: The narrator's father
characters.description: Deceased (his death certificate is in Mamá's drawer); in flashback read the school letter twice in the kitchen and said only 'Nivel dos.' Physical appearance unspecified.
characters.evidence:
He said one word, which was the number on it, in Spanish, the way you say the number of a bus
you’re not going to take.

characters.name: Mamá
characters.description: In flashback, took the school letter and put it in the drawer of papers that matter without another word; keeps the lease, the father's death certificate, and unanswered school letters there. Physical appearance unspecified.
characters.evidence:
My mother took the letter and put it in the drawer where she keeps
the papers that matter:

characters.name: Mikey
characters.description: Mentioned-only; childhood friend who 'lived on four'; pressed his ear to the fourth-floor stairwell wall and said the building was humming; JC now thinks he was accurate. Physical appearance unspecified.
characters.evidence:
Mikey used to press his ear to the wall of the fourth-floor stairwell
and tell me the building was humming.

characters.name: Mikey's mother
characters.description: Mentioned-only; said 'the three' most often, in a particular voice, like a rumor or a diagnosis. Physical appearance unspecified.

characters.name: The mothers on the block
characters.description: Mentioned-only collective; referred to the Calm Index scores as 'the three' in a particular voice. Physical appearance unspecified.
characters.evidence:
I remembered what the mothers on the block
called it.

characters.name: Don Chino
characters.description: Mentioned-only; owner of the bodega with the faded orange-soda awning and the speaker over the door. Physical appearance unspecified.
characters.evidence: Don Chino’s bodega has an awning the color of a faded orange soda,

characters.name: The domino players outside the bodega
characters.description: Unnamed ensemble: two guys on milk crates slapping domino tiles and arguing, and a third who steps out of the shop to tell them to lower their voices in a voice that isn't lower; the flatness goes out of all three within a minute. Physical appearance unspecified.
characters.evidence:
Two guys sat on milk crates out front with a domino table, slap‐
ping tiles, in the mood to argue.

scenes.name: Vending-machine lunch at the Concourse library
scenes.description: JC eats platanitos and a ginger ale from a vending machine at 2:15 by the radiator beside a snoring man; his phone buzzes with Sofía's escalating texts about the 'is this anything' email and Denise's message that the board is holding his milestone payment, with nine days to rent.
scenes.evidence:
I ate lunch at 2:15, in the library, from a vending machine, which I
want on the record as technically a meal.

scenes.name: Researching the cemí and the coin
scenes.description: Supposed to be fixing the mural he broke on purpose, JC instead searches spirals and finds a museum cemí — a three-pointed dark stone with a face and a spiral-triangle — matching the coin his grandmother gave him at twelve.
scenes.evidence:
a
three-pointed stone, dark, fist-sized, with a face carved into the front
and a spiral that opened into a triangle on the back.

scenes.name: Flashback: the bundle in the closet in Santo Domingo
scenes.description: Memory of the only visit JC remembers, at eight: his grandmother's bundle wrapped in old cloth in the back of her closet; she caught his wrist gently — 'No se toca a la Madre' — and gave him a mango.
scenes.evidence:
My grandmother keeps a bundle in the back of her closet in Santo
Domingo, wrapped in old cloth, about the size of two cupped hands.

scenes.name: ECHO: the Concourse reading room, 1934
scenes.description: JC sets the contact mic puck on the oak table to check Chismosa; the radiator, snorer and buzzing lamp line up and the room fills with a Saturday reading room circa 1934 — green lamps, a multilingual crowd, a leaking rumba, a FREE CONCERT sign — with no flat spot under the sound; he nearly cries before Sofía's arrival snaps the room back.

scenes.name: Sofía's Aperture Civic briefing
scenes.description: Sofía sits down laptop-first and lays out Aperture Civic: registered 2024, three shells, a holding company owning a youth digital-wellness nonprofit, a music-licensing outfit, and a development group with permits on four buildings including JC's; the June thirteenth Founders' Night deadline at the Armory; and the only findable human, Adrian Vale with his black notebook.

scenes.name: The loop, the earbud, and the need for a control
scenes.description: JC plays Sofía the eight-second loop saved from the raw feed; she believes he heard something but demands numbers and a control block without it, revealing the music-licensing arm's free in-store systems installed in six nearby businesses for two months.
scenes.evidence:
“That’s a loop,” she said. “It sounds like every hold music in Amer‐
ica.”

scenes.name: The café that didn't sign
scenes.description: Sofía reveals every business signed the same page-and-a-half contract except one — the café, where Mr. Rodríguez refused the speaker and plays his own records — giving them a control; Sofía is briefly, completely happy.
scenes.evidence: “I’m in love with a coffee shop,” she said.

scenes.name: The Quiet Hours Foundation, 2007
scenes.description: About twenty minutes later, Sofía traces the shared registered-agent address backward to the Quiet Hours Foundation's Early Calm Pilot final report: a 2007 grant putting ambient tones and a screening tool in four elementary schools in JC's zip code — the schools JC attended.
scenes.evidence:
Quiet Hours Foundation. Early Calm Pilot: Final
Report. 2007.

scenes.name: Flashback: quiet time and the letter home
scenes.description: JC remembers the beige speaker above the cubbies, the flat tone after lunch, his desk-tapping to push back; the woman with the lanyard and clipboard; the letter his father read twice and answered with 'Nivel dos'; his mother filing it in the drawer without another word.
scenes.evidence:
It sat on top of the supply closet, a beige box with a mesh front, right
above the cubbies.

scenes.name: The Calm Index rubric and memories of Mikey
scenes.description: Sofía reads the Calm Index rubric — 'Atypical response to ambient stimulus' — the line you write to find the kids who react; JC remembers Mikey, who lived on four, pressing his ear to the stairwell wall, and the mothers calling scores 'the three.'
scenes.evidence: That’s a sentence you write when you’re looking for the kids who react.

scenes.name: Sofía's warning: the model has to be right
scenes.description: Sofía concludes someone has had a model of the block since JC was six and that people who need to be right don't stop; she tells him not to reply to the email, not to delete it, and not to walk home past the bodega.
scenes.evidence:
“Don’t reply to the email,” she said finally. “Don’t delete it. And
don’t walk home past the bodega.”

scenes.name: Walking home past the bodega
scenes.description: JC defies the warning and stops to listen on purpose outside Don Chino's bodega: under a bright merengue he hears the pressed-down eight-second loop in the open air, and watches the flatness pass through three domino players in under a minute.
scenes.evidence: I stood on the sidewalk and listened to it on purpose.
